Wartime Propaganda in Canada
 Education Guides | 2026
This guide invites students to explore Canadian propaganda posters from the Second World War through critical thinking activities.

Canada's Government Structure Posters
 Education Guides | 2026
Designed as printable posters to be hung in classrooms, this resource uses key terms and descriptive flow charts to outline the main features of Canadian federal government.

 Women in Canadian History | 2026

 Maple Moments | 2026

Fighting Against Death: Canadian Medical Personnel in Afghanistan
 The Memory Project | 2026
From 2001 to 2014, Canadian Armed Forces medical personnel served in Afghanistan, providing life-saving care in active combat zones, under constant threat of fire.

 Maple Moments | 2025

Anne Innis Dagg
 Heritage Minutes | 2025
In 1956, Dr. Anne Innis Dagg became the first Western researcher to study any mammal in the wild in Africa. She is still known as one of the foremost experts on giraffes.

Voices of Victory: Remembering VE Day
 The Memory Project | 2025
To mark the 80th anniversary of VE Day, eight veterans of the war remember how they learned of victory, and how they celebrated the momentous occasion.

A Heritage Minute Salute to Canada Day
 Heritage Minutes | 2025
Historica Canada presents a salute to Canada Day pairing The Hip’s “It’s a Good Life (If You Don’t Weaken’)” with scenes from the Heritage Minutes

Bora Laskin
 Heritage Minutes | 2025
One of Canada’s greatest legal scholars, Bora Laskin overcame antisemitism to become the first Jewish Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Canada.

War Artists Resource Kit
 Education Guides | 2025

The Vikings
 Citizenship Challenge | 2025
Norse Sagas and archaeological findings at L’Anse aux Meadows in Newfoundland come together to reveal the history of the first European presence in Canada.

Edwin A. Baker
 Heritage Minutes | 2024
After losing his sight during the First World War, Edwin A. Baker co-founded the Canadian National Institute for the Blind.

Mary Riter Hamilton
 Heritage Minutes | 2024
Mary Riter Hamilton painted the battlefields after the First World War as a testament to its devastating cost. She would suffer mental and physical illnesses as a result of documenting the experiences of Canadian soldiers.

The Forgotten Navy: The Merchant Navy in the Second World War
 The Memory Project | 2024

Dinosaurs Found in Canada
 The Canadian Encyclopedia | 2024

Abraham Ulrikab and Human Zoos
 The Canadian Encyclopedia | 2024

Prohibition and the Yukon
 Citizenship Challenge | 2024
Amidst Canada’s Prohibition period in the 20th century, the Yukon found itself at the heart of national and international affairs, with lasting implications on land and in the skies.
